Ngunnawal and Gundungurra are very closely related and the two were most likely highly mutually intelligible. As such they can be considered dialects of a single unnamed language, but this is the technical linguistic usage of these terms and Ngunnawal and Gundungurra peoples prefer to describe their individual varieties as separate languages in their own right.{{Cite book| chapter = Aboriginal languages and social groups in the Canberra region: interpreting the historical documentation | last1 = Gundungurra/Ngunawal is generally classified to fall within the tentative (and perhaps geographic) [[Yuin–Kuric languages|Yuin–Kuric group]] of the [[Pama–Nyungan languages|Pama–Nyungan family]].{{cite web|url=http://www1.aiatsis.gov.au/thesaurus/language/mtw.exe?k=default&l=60&s=1&n=1&y=0&w=Ngunawal%2B%2F%2BNgunnawal%2Blanguage%2B%28D3%29%2B%28NSW%2BSI55%2D16%29&t=3|title=AIATSIS March 2011}} ==Geographical distribution== The traditional country of the Ngunnawal people is generally thought to have extended east near [[Goulburn]], North to [[Boorowa]], south through Canberra, perhaps even to Queanbeyan, and extending west to around the [[Goodradigbee River]]. == Current status == The language was [[Extinct language|extinct]] by 1994.{{Cite book |last=Moseley |first=Christopher |title=Atlas of the world's languages |last2=Asher |first2=Ronald E. |date=1994 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-0-415-01925-5 |location=London}} Some recordings of the last native speakers exist, but they did not bring their children up to speak the language. The Ngunnawal community has for some years been engaged in work to revive the language, aiming to bring it back into daily use within the community. They have been working with [[Australian Institute of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Studies|AIATSIS]] linguists to assist them with this work, and with identifying historical records that can be used.{{Cite journal |last=Marmion |first=Douglas |author-link=Douglas Marmion |year=2015 |title=Bringing back the Ngunawal language |journal=[[Australian Aboriginal Studies]] |volume=2 |pages=65–69}} == Phonology == {| class="IPA wikitable" style="text-align: center;" |+Ngunawal consonants{{cite web|url=http://www.green-ebook-shop.com/ebooks/1/8/9/7/18978/18978.html|archive-url=https://archive.today/20131011230749/http://www.green-ebook-shop.com/ebooks/1/8/9/7/18978/18978.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=2013-10-11|title=The Wiradyuri and Other Languages of New South Wales|author=Robert Hamilton Mathews}} ! !
